true_answer: We will use the notation f ( A ) to denote the image of A under f , namely the set of elements in Y that are the image of elements from A . That is, f ( A ) | { f ( a )∈ Y : a ∈ A } . We can do this in the other direction as well. We might ask which elements of the domain get mapped to a particular set in the codomain. Let f : X → Y be a function and suppose B ⊆ Y is a subset of the codomain. Then we will write f − 1 ( B ) for the inverse image of B under f , namely the set of elements in X whose image are elements in B . In other words, f − 1 ( B ) | { x ∈ X : f ( x )∈ B } .
